author: austen
text: Her performance was agreeable, though not outstanding. After a song or two and before she could answer the various entreaties to sing again, she yielded the instrument eagerly to her sister Mary, who, being the only plain sister in the family and thus eager to acquire knowledge and accomplishments, was perpetually eager for an opportunity to display them.

author: austen
text: Elizabeth rejoined them only to say that her sister was worse and that she could not leave her. Bingley urged that Mr. Jones be sent for immediately; while his sisters, convinced that no country remedy could be effective, recommended an express to town for one of the most eminent physicians. This she would not hear of; yet she was not entirely unwilling to accede to her brother’s proposal, and it was settled that Mr. Jones should be dispatched early the following morning should Miss Bennet not be decidedly better. Bingley was quite uncomfortable; his sisters declared themselves miserable. They assuaged their wretchedness by singing duets after supper, while he found relief in giving his housekeeper instructions to ensure every possible attention to the sick lady and her sister.

author: austen
text: “Nay,” cried Bingley, “this is too much—to remember at night all the foolish things that were said in the morning. And yet, upon my honor, I believed what I said of myself to be true, and I believe it at this moment. At least, therefore, I did not assume the character of needless precipitance merely to show off before the ladies.”

author: austen
text: “Pride,” said Miss Lucas, “is justifiable here. A fine young man, with fortune, might deem himself entitled to it.”

author: austen
text: “I know you do,” she continued, “and that is what makes the wonder. With your good sense, to be so honestly blind to the follies and nonsense of others! Affectation of candour is common enough; one meets it everywhere. But to be candid without ostentation or design—to seize the good in everyone’s character and enhance it, while saying nothing of the bad—that is a gift reserved for you alone. And so, you like this man’s sisters, too, do you? Their manners are not equal to his.”
